DKSAP-IoT is a faster dual-key stealth address protocol for blockchain-based IoT systems.
DKSAP-IoT reduces computational overhead by at least 50% compared to the state-of-the-art scheme.
DKSAP-IoT uses a cryptographic hash function to extend the lifetime of the shared secret between senders and receivers.
DKSAP-IoT reduces the number of random-point scalar multiplications (RP) and fixed-point scalar multiplications (FP) required for each stealth transaction.
The overall cost of DKSAP-IoT is less than 50% of DKSAP.
DKSAP-IoT provides strong anonymity for receivers and ensures the unlinkability of payments received by the same payee.
The threat model of DKSAP-IoT is that an adversary aims to determine the corresponding recipients by observing the transactions on the blockchain.
The computational overhead of DKSAP is N * 2 RP and N * 2 FP.
The communication overhead of DKSAP is N elliptic curve points.
The hash function used in DKSAP-IoT is BLAKE-256.

The performance of DKSAP-IoT on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B is that the computation of the hash function is about three orders of magnitude faster than that of the scalar multiplication over an elliptic curve.
The implementation of DKSAP-IoT is an optimized elliptic curve cryptography library, namely libsect283k11, which is written in C and compiled using the GNU C Compiler (GCC).
The timings for the computation of RP, FP, and H on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B are 3.67 ms, 3.12 ms, and 5.26 µs, respectively.
The library used in the implementation of DKSAP-IoT is libsect283k1, which is an optimized elliptic curve cryptography library.
The library is written in C and compiled using the GNU C Compiler (GCC).
The library uses the lambda coordinates, the window τNAF method, pre-computation, and other efficient techniques to optimize performance.
